clues: This city sits in the heart of a dry land in south west Africa. It stands on a high, flat plain in the middle of that land.
This dry land city gets more than three hundred days of sun each year. High ground keeps its heat mild, but rain comes mostly in summer.
A German army major built this city up a second time in 1890. He led the troops who had just claimed the land for the German Empire.
The city first grew by a hot spring that herding tribes knew well. A captain settled there in 1840 and built a stone church.
This is the capital of Namibia, the seat of its leaders and firms. Most big offices and schools of the land are based in this city.
